This application coming on for order this day, the court passed the following:
 ORDER
This is the second application under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. for grant of bail.
First application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 17.10.2022 passed in M.Cr.C.No.48078 of 2022.

The applicant has been arrested on 11.06.2022 by Police Station - Indergarh, District Datia (M.P.) in connection with Crime No.107/2022 registered in relation to the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366-A, 376-D, 323, 342, 506, 201 of IPC and Section 3/4, 5/6 and 17 of POCSO Act.

sentences.text: As per prosecution story, family of the prosecutrix is well known to the family of the accused persons Ashish and Dashrath and present applicant Daulat.

It is alleged that while the prosecutrix had gone to Anganbadi Kendra to collect her meals and was coming back, as the Kendra was closed,
on the way of Dabra- Indergarh, she was forced to sit inside a white Bolero car and she was administered some eatable resulting into her unconsciousness.
When she woke up, she found herself in Gujarat.
The alleged incident is of 28/03/2022.
She has been recovered on 19/05/2022 at Gwalior Railway Station.
Accordingly, the case has been registered.
During the course of investigation, her statements under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C. were recorded.

In her statement under Section 161 of Cr.P.C she has alleged against main accused Mahesh and Abhishek, who after kidnapping had taken her to Gujarat where she was kept for one and half months and subjected to sexual abuse by both of them.
However, she did not mention the name of the present applicant Daulat or accused Dashrath.
But in her statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. she has also included their name with the allegation that they had beaten her while she was sitting in Bolero car.
In the court statement recorded on 12/10/2022 she has not mentioned the name of the applicant or that of Dashrath.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that involvement of applicant and that of Dashrath is case of false implication.
They are uncles of main accused Abhishek.
Their names were never mentioned either in the FIR or in the 161 statement or for that matter in the court statement.

As a matter of fact, there are differences between the families of the accused and prosecutrix as the house sold to the accused long ago was sought to be taken back from him owing to rise of prices of the house.
The assertion in that behalf was given by the mother of the prosecutrix (P.W.2) in para 4 of her statement, therefore, it is a case of false implication.
It is submitted that applicant Daulat is aged about 35 years.
He has no criminal 3 of 4 antecedents.
Charge sheet has been filed, therefore, no custodial interrogation is required.
Conclusion of Trial is likely to take time.
Under such circumstances, applicant may be given the benefit of bail.
Per contra, Smt. Anjali Gyanani, learned Public Prosecutor for the State, opposes the application.
She reiterated the fact that name of the applicant appeared in the statement of the prosecutrix under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., therefore, complicity of the applicant can not be ruled out.
However, she fairly submits that as his name does not appear either in the statement of the prosecutrix under Section 161 or court statement.
The DNA report is also not against the applicant.

Upon hearing learned counsel for the rival parties but without commenting upon the rival contentions touching merits of the case, regard being had to the fact that the applicant is in custody since 11.6.2022 with no criminal antecedents, not required for custodial investigation as challan has been filed, hence, the applicant is held entitled for enlargement on bail.
Consequently, the application of the applicant filed under Section 439 of the Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 is hereby allowed.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail on furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakh only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Trial Court and on the condition that he shall remain present before the Court concerned during trial and also comply with the conditions enumerated Daulat vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145289125/
2 under Section 437 (3) of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 with following further conditions:
(i) the applicant shall mark his attendance before the concerned police station on 02nd and 04th Saturday every month between 10:00 a.m. to 12:00 noon.
(ii) the applicant shall abide by the terms and conditions of various circulars and orders issued by the Government of India and the State Government as well as 4 of 4 the local administration from time-to-time in the matter of maintaining social distancing, physical distancing, hygiene, etc., to avoid proliferation of Novel Corona virus (COVID-19);
(iii) the concerned jail authorities are directed that before releasing the applicant, the medical examination of the applicant be conducted through the jail doctor and if it is prima facie found that he is having any symptoms of COVID-19, then the consequential follow up action or any further test required, be undertaken immediately.
